content:
The [FPS Converter](/fps-converter) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Convert frames per second to frame time, Hz, frames per minute and more. Enter your frames per second (fps) and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

Convert a frame rate in frames per second into everything it implies: how long each frame lasts in milliseconds, the frequency in hertz, and how many frames that means per minute and per hour. 60 fps is 16.67 ms per frame — the budget every frame has in a 60 Hz game or video. The same rate as a frequency is simply 60 Hz, because one frame per second is one cycle per second.

## How to use the FPS Converter

Start by entering your frames per second (fps). The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause. The steps below walk through each input in order.

1. Enter the frame rate in frames per second.
2. Read the frame time in milliseconds — the budget each frame has.
3. See the same rate as a frequency and as frames per minute and hour.

## Formula

Frame time = 1,000 ÷ fps (milliseconds). Frequency = fps Hz. Frames per minute = fps × 60. Frames per hour = fps × 3,600.

That is the standard formula for this calculation, and it is the same one the [FPS Converter](/fps-converter) applies to the values you enter. You can work it out by hand, but the calculator is faster when you want to try several values, and it removes the risk of a slip in the arithmetic.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. At 60 fps each frame lasts 16.67 ms, the frequency is 60 Hz, and there are 3,600 frames per minute and 216,000 per hour. At 24 fps — the cinema standard — each frame lasts 41.67 ms. Try the same figures in the [FPS Converter](/fps-converter) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves.

## What the result shows

With the default values (Frames per second (fps): 60), the [FPS Converter](/fps-converter) returns Frame time: 16.67 ms per frame, Frequency: 60 Hz, Frames per minute: 3,600, Frames per hour: 216,000, Seconds per 1,000 frames: 16.67 s. The first figure is the headline result, and the rest break it down so you can see how the total is made up. If you want to compare with a related calculation, the [Temperature Converter](/temperature-converter) is worth a look before you finish.

## Why frame time matters

Gamers and video engineers think in frame time, not fps, because frame time is what the hardware must achieve: at 60 fps every frame must render in 16.67 ms, and a single 33 ms frame is a visible stutter even if the average stays at 60. At 144 fps the budget is just 6.94 ms per frame, and at 30 fps it is a comfortable 33.33 ms. Averages hide stutters; frame times show them.

## Common frame rates

Cinema runs at 24 fps, television at 25 (PAL) or 30 (NTSC) fps, and most games target 60 fps, with competitive play at 120 or 144 fps and high-refresh monitors reaching 240 fps. A 24 fps film shown on a 60 Hz screen repeats frames in a 3:2 pattern, which is why film can look slightly juddery on a TV — the frame times do not divide evenly.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Frame time is the honest number: 16.67 ms per frame is what 60 fps really means.
- To halve the frame time you must double the frame rate — 120 fps is 8.33 ms per frame.
- Cinema's 24 fps gives each frame 41.67 ms — slow by gaming standards, but film hides it with motion blur.

## Frequently asked questions

### How many milliseconds is 60 fps?

16.67 ms per frame — 1,000 ÷ 60. Each frame in a 60 fps game or video must be ready within that time. Try it with your own numbers in the [FPS Converter](/fps-converter) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Is fps the same as Hz?

Numerically, yes: 60 frames per second is a frequency of 60 Hz. But Hz describes the display's refresh rate while fps describes the content — a 60 fps game on a 144 Hz screen still shows 60 frames a second. Try it with your own numbers in the [FPS Converter](/fps-converter) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What fps do films use?

24 fps, the cinema standard for nearly a century. Television uses 25 or 30 fps, and games usually target 60 fps or more. Try it with your own numbers in the [FPS Converter](/fps-converter) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What formula does the FPS Converter use?

Frame time = 1,000 ÷ fps (milliseconds). Frequency = fps Hz. Frames per minute = fps × 60. Frames per hour = fps × 3,600. You can see it in action in the [FPS Converter](/fps-converter) — enter your own values and the result updates as you type.
